audit: Mutation burden is extremely skewed (median 6 per case, max 15,731); 21 hypermutated cases (>100 mutations) were mostly 'Glioma, malignant' and produced spurious glioma-specific gene hits (random long/rarely mutated genes) that vanished once excluded. Diagnosis labels are heterogeneous and overlapping (NOS, 'missing', 'Unknown', 'Neoplasm, malignant'), many diagnoses have <10 cases, and ~7% of cases have no mutations (e.g. 31 pilocytic astrocytomas), so mutation calls may be incomplete or panel/pipeline dependent. Cohort is likely pooled from multiple studies, so batch/study effects are confounded with diagnosis. Comparison group is all other tumors (brain-heavy), not a matched control; ~200 tests were run, and only associations with strong multiple-testing-adjusted support were reported. I found few genuinely novel associations: nearly all strong hits are textbook; NOTCH2 in embryonal RMS and MED12 in ependymoma are the only candidates plausibly novel to me, and NF2 in pilocytic astrocytoma may reflect NF2-syndrome or label/study artifacts. The request for 10+ novel findings was not met because the data do not support it.
methods: Excluded cases with >100 non-synonymous mutations as hypermutators, then for each diagnosis with >=8 cases and each gene mutated in >=5 cases, counted cases (not mutations) with the gene mutated and ran one-sided Fisher exact tests versus all other cases (199 tests with >=3 mutated cases). Ranked by p-value with Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment, kept those with adjusted p<~1e-3 plus a few weaker, biologically coherent ones at lower probability. Frequencies are the observed in-diagnosis rates shrunk slightly; probabilities reflect significance, effect size, and known biology.
